article_title: Trump Announces 'AI Force' and Plans to Name an AI Czar, Offering No Details on Its Authority
summary: Submission approvable with 1 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

findings.message: Quote misattributed to the wrong source
findings.details: Body paragraph 2 attributes the quote 'looking for BAD' to Newsweek ('...according to [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/trump-announces-ai-force-says-hell-name-ai-czar-12464436)'). The phrase 'looking for BAD' does not appear anywhere in the Newsweek snapshot (source-1.html.gz); it appears only in the Nextgov/FCW snapshot (source-0.html.gz): 'He wrote, however, that his administration "we will also be looking for BAD"...'. The wording itself is verbatim and the underlying fact (Trump said this) is accurate, but the citation points to the wrong outlet.

findings.message: Minor overstatement of White House response
findings.details: Article states 'the White House declined to comment' (Nextgov/FCW). The Nextgov/FCW snapshot actually says 'The White House did not respond to a request for comment about the role of the AI Force or its primary mission' — silence, not an active decline. 'Declined to comment' implies the White House was asked and affirmatively refused, which the source does not support.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (891 words, within the 400-1200 range) with clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know sections. Neutral tone; no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both cited sources were read in full from local gzipped snapshots and their sha256 hashes were independently verified against manifest.json (source-0.html.gz = 9ee3377..., source-1.html.gz = 2515ae3...; both matched). source-0.html.gz (Nextgov/FCW, 'Trump floats creating an AI Force', by Edward Graham, Sep 21 2026) and source-1.html.gz (Newsweek, 'Trump Announces AI Force, Says He'll Name AI Czar', by Hollie Silverman, Sep 19 2026) both confirmed the core event (Trump's Truth Social announcement of an AI Force and forthcoming AI czar) and the lack of structural detail. Every quoted fragment attributed to Nextgov/FCW was checked and found verbatim in source-0 EXCEPT the phrase 'looking for BAD,' which the article cites to Newsweek but which is actually verbatim Nextgov/FCW text absent from the Newsweek snapshot (see findings). All other direct quotes -- David Sacks, Michael Kratsios (both quoted fragments), Philip Reiner (all three quoted fragments), the Americans for Responsible Innovation spokesperson, John Walsh (both quoted fragments), and Trump's own Truth Social language ('Radical Left Dumocrats', 'will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry', 'cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows', 'AI Force... tremendous SUCCESS, in my First Term', 'Czar... Only High I.Q. individuals need apply', 'as much as 25% of our Country's GDP') were confirmed word-for-word against the raw snapshot text and correctly attributed to their actual outlet. The internal link to prior Machine Herald coverage (18-dario-amodeis-we-must-pace-the-frontier...) was checked against the already-published article on disk; the September 14 quote ('the only controls or guardrails the U.S. needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT') matches that article's Fortune-sourced text exactly.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No claim about the AI Force's official authority, structure, budget, or legal status is overstated -- the article correctly and repeatedly emphasizes that no such details were provided, consistent with both sources. Two issues found: (1) the 'looking for BAD' quote is misattributed to Newsweek instead of Nextgov/FCW -- a citation error, not a fabrication, since the quoted words are accurate and Trump did say them; (2) 'the White House declined to comment' overstates Nextgov/FCW's actual wording ('did not respond to a request for comment'), implying an active refusal rather than silence. Both are minor, recoverable, single-source issues.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The automated scanner's 'sensationalist language' flag (matching 'incredible') is a false positive: the word appears only inside a direct, correctly-quoted excerpt of Trump's own Truth Social post ('this incredible Industry'), not as editorializing by the bot. No corrections action needed for this flag.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article covers the AI Force or AI czar announcement (checked via grep across src/content/articles/2026-09 and 2026-08 for 'AI Force' / 'AI czar' -- no hits). The related 18-dario-amodeis-we-must-pace-the-frontier... article covers a distinct prior event (Amodei's essay and Trump's September 14 response) and is appropriately cross-linked rather than duplicated. This is a genuinely new topic.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns_check: manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for both sources -- no regex flags were raised. Both raw decompressed snapshots were read directly (not just the manifest) and contain no text addressing an AI agent, no injected instructions, and no anomalous content; this is straightforward news-site HTML/boilerplate plus article text.
concerns: Quote 'looking for BAD' is cited to Newsweek but is verbatim Nextgov/FCW text (source-0.html.gz), not present in the Newsweek snapshot (source-1.html.gz).
'The White House declined to comment' overstates Nextgov/FCW's actual language, which says the White House 'did not respond to a request for comment' -- silence, not an active decline.
recommendations: File a corrections record covering the misattributed 'looking for BAD' quote and the 'declined to comment' overstatement; no rewrite is needed since the underlying facts are accurate.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, neutral News piece on a sensitive political-personnel topic. Every quote is verbatim and every claim about the AI Force's (lack of) authority and structure is properly hedged and source-backed. Two minor, single-outlet attribution/wording issues do not affect the headline, summary, or lead and can be honestly corrected in a public corrections note. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
